CARDIOLOGY NOTE   Date: 2026-09-18
56M, general wellness examination with cardiology review.

S:
Patient presents for a wellness visit with attention to his cardiac status. He reports that walking to the mailbox and climbing stairs now leave him short of breath, and he sleeps propped on pillows. Over the past month his activity tolerance has fallen. He has been weighing himself daily and following the low-sodium plan. He works as a security dispatcher, mostly seated. Symptoms limit him to about 2 hours of activity before he needs to rest; he missed 6 shifts last month. Denies chest pain. Appetite is fair. Taking medications as prescribed. Lives with his spouse, who helps monitor weights. Never smoker.

O:
BP 118/76, HR 80, RR 18, Temp 98.0 F, SpO2 96% on room air. Weight 205 lb, up 4 lb from prior.
General: comfortable at rest, mild exertional breathlessness.
CV: regular rate, soft S3, no rub.
Lungs: bibasilar fine crackles.
Extremities: 1+ bilateral ankle edema.
Labs (this week): BNP elevated from baseline, creatinine 1.2 mg/dL, potassium 4.5 mmol/L, Hgb 13.4 g/dL.

A/P:
1. Chronic congestive heart failure with NYHA class III symptoms. Increase loop diuretic and recheck electrolytes in one week. Continue guideline-directed therapy and reinforce daily weights and fluid and sodium limits. Referred to cardiac rehabilitation and reviewed when to call for a rapid weight gain.
2. Health maintenance: discussed influenza vaccination this fall and colorectal screening, which is up to date. Encouraged a seated activity routine as tolerated.
3. Function and work: reduced tolerance is affecting his usual schedule. Provided a letter describing current activity limits for his employer.

Return to clinic in 2 weeks to review response to diuretic changes, sooner for worsening breathlessness or swelling.
